significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that, among internally correct factual-recall failures, late components tracking "token frequency, recency, string similarity to the subject" causally defeat retrieved facts according to the "strength gap between the retrieved-fact direction and the heuristic direction," and that suppressing those components restores correct answers. This combines a mechanistic causal decomposition with a form-(iii) predictive win condition, fixing expectations for which future QA cases will fail rather than merely showing that facts are decodable; it would sharpen the staged-recall account studied in Geva et al.'s 2023 work on dissecting factual recall. The phenomenon is a knowing-versus-saying dissociation and the mechanism is late heuristic arbitration; a negative result would rule out a compact override mechanism for the selected failures, though not all suppression accounts, and the vague qualifiers "some failures" and "a measurable fraction" modestly weaken determinacy. After topic substitution, the broad question of why stored knowledge fails would not retain this score—the specific two-signal win condition and causal override are what raise it above the topic-median probe-and-ablation hypothesis.

reach.justification: The claim supplies two named handles: the measurable "strength gap between the retrieved-fact direction and the heuristic direction" and the intervention of "ablating or down-weighting" override components. The gap is potentially an ex-ante predictor immediately before token emission, while the intervention is a decode-time control, but the action window is short and the hypothesis does not assert applicability across architectures or model families. After re-extraction, the proposed gap relation could predict which factual-QA cases fail, whereas the particular components and directions must be rediscovered per model; likely downstream users are interpretability researchers and, if collateral error remains low, model auditors or deployment engineers. Topic substitution leaves no such diagnostic or intervention, so the score comes from the claim, although its unstated cross-model scope keeps its reach near the topic's default deliverable rather than in the broad-transfer band.
